## Familiar statistics · Interquartile range {#l2-stat-iqr .quick-stat}

The interquartile range measures the spread of the middle half of the ordered data.

```{=html}
<p class="number-list-label">The same 10 numbers, in order:</p>
<div class="number-strip" aria-label="1, 2, 2, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6, 8, 10"><span class="stat-number">1</span><span class="stat-number">2</span><span class="stat-number stat-focus">2</span><span class="stat-number">4</span><span class="stat-number">5</span><span class="stat-number">6</span><span class="stat-number">6</span><span class="stat-number stat-focus">6</span><span class="stat-number">8</span><span class="stat-number">10</span></div>
```

Subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile.

$$
\mathrm{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1=6-2=4
$$

::: notes
Keep this familiar-statistics reminder quick: one statistic and one worked calculation per slide. Use the same ordered dataset throughout. Its sum is 50, n=10, mean=5, median=5.5, mode=6, range=9, Q1=2, Q3=6 and IQR=4. For odd samples, use the school convention of excluding the overall median when taking medians of the two halves.
:::
